 This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 03.02.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.496/2013 by the II Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kolar ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.text: II Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kolar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, the brother petitioner by name Adigi Mahendra @ T.Chinna, the deceased, on 02.07.2012 at about 8.30 p.m., while walking on the footpath of Bangarupalem on NC:
2023:KHC:40995 Palamaner-Chittoor road, hit by a Tractor bearing No.AP-20/T-2935 killing him at the spot.
The petitioner being the unmarried dependant sister of the deceased approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation.
The claim was opposed by the owner and insurer of the Tractor.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal awarded Rs.8,25,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt.Suguna R.Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.A.M.Venkatesh, learned counsel for Insurance Company.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that both petitioner and deceased were unmarried, they are residing together and interdependent to each other.

The Tribunal while considering the assessment of compensation did not NC: 2023:KHC:40995 consider the future prospects and assessed less compensation, so also compensation under the conventional heads and sought for enhancement.

entities.text: Kumari Revathi vs Sri V Venkatesh Redy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner is major sister and she is not the dependant, but the Tribunal has assessed the compensation as dependant,
which is not correct.
Utmost the petitioner is entitled to loss of estate and the income assessed at Rs.7,500/- per month is higher than what has been assessed for a person with no proof of income in the year 2012.

Hence, he sought that compensation be calculated taking the income at Rs.7,000/-
instead of Rs.7,500/- taken by the Tribunal.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased on account of accidental injuries.
Petitioner is the younger sister of the deceased.
The deceased was aged 28 years on the date of accident.
The material on record did point out that both are unmarried, they resided together.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.ltd. -vs- Birender and Others1 laid down at para-15 that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.ltd. -vs- Birender and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.
AIR 2020 SC 434 NC: 2023:KHC:40995 9.
The evidence on record points out that the petitioner being the unmarried sister is dependant of her brother.
Hence, petitioner being the unmarried younger sister of the deceased being legal representative and dependant is entitled to maintain the claim petition.
The argument on behalf of the Insurance Company is not persuasive that the petitioner is entitled only to the compensation under conventional heads.
10. The petitioner has not produced any material in proof of the avocation and income of the deceased.

Though the deceased was stated to be a mason aged 28 years as per the medical records,
he has to be treated as a person with no proof of income.
In the year 2012, notional income of a person with no proof of income is assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month, accordingly, it has to be taken.
For the age of '27', the multiplier applicable NC: 2023:KHC:40995 is '17' and 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

11. In a case of this nature, compensation has to be determined by following the principles settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others2 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another3 so also the principle laid down in Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd. - Vs- Bhagat Singh Rawat & Ors.4 Kumari Revathi vs Sri V Venkatesh Redy on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170194011/
3 12.

sentences.text: By following the said principles, compensation has to be determined.

Under the conventional heads, a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection and towards funeral expenses and loss of (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 Civil Appeal Nos.2410-2412/2023, decided on 27.03.2023 NC: 2023:KHC:40995 estate at Rs.15,000/- each,
amounting to Rs.80,000/-. Since the claim is of the year 2013, in view of the judgment in Bhagat Singh Rawat's case (supra), 10% has to be added for every three years.
If so assessed, it comes to Rs.24,000/-.
The petitioner is entitled to Rs.1,04,000/- under the conventional heads.

If it is added,
total compensation comes to Rs.11,03,600/- as against Rs.8,25,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,78,600/-, which is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified;

(iii) The petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,78,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on NC: 2023:KHC:40995 the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization;
(iv) Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact;
(v) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
SD/-
